title: ALLMod: Exploring \underline{A}rea-Efficiency of \underline{L}UT-based \underline{L}arge Number \underline{Mod}ular Reduction via Hybrid Workloads
problem: LUT-based large-number modular reduction incurs substantial area overhead.
method_or_artifact: Split bit groups into hybrid workloads using a balancing template; explore when to fuse workload results.
workload_or_benchmark: Modular reduction at 128- and 8192-bit widths; HE and ZKP are motivating applications, not established end-to-end benchmarks.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: LUT-based hardware; device, process, clock and implementation type unspecified.
baselines: Conventional LUT-based methods; exact implementations unspecified

metrics.condition: 128-bit modular reduction versus conventional LUT-based methods; efficiency definition and area/throughput accounting unspecified
8192-bit modular reduction versus conventional LUT-based methods; not an end-to-end HE/ZKP speedup

classification_rationale: Hardware arithmetic is primary; design-space exploration is a supporting method, not evidence of AI-assisted EDA.
limits: Description claims throughput is preserved but gives no absolute throughput, device, resource accounting or experiment budget. No cryptographic security validation is established.

workload_or_benchmark: Sequential circuits, including larger circuits; corpus identities and train/test split unspecified.
baselines: Existing circuit learning methods; specific models unspecified

title: PastATPG: A Hybrid ATPG Framework for Better Test Compaction with Partial Assignment SAT
problem: Complete SAT assignments inflate ATPG patterns and impede compaction.
method_or_artifact: PA-MiniSat generates partial assignments using full-literal watching and circuit-adapted branching; PastATPG integrates structural and SAT algorithms in test compaction.
workload_or_benchmark: ATPG, particularly hard-to-detect faults; circuit suites and fault models unspecified.
classification_rationale: SAT is used for manufacturing-test compaction, not general formal proof; testing branch is primary.
limits: Only qualitative improvements are reported. Commercial speed advantage is limited to some cases; no numeric speedup, pattern reduction, fault coverage parity or universal dominance is established.
Official description only; no full-text extraction or independent reproduction.
